html:
On 8 May 1945, the day the war in Europe ended, a march of Algerians in Sétif carrying nationalist flags turned into a riot in which about a hundred Europeans were killed. French forces answered with weeks of massacre around Sétif and Guelma.

Soldiers, police and settler militias killed thousands of Algerians; estimates run from a few thousand to tens of thousands. Villages were bombed from the air and shelled from warships.

Many Algerians had fought for France in the Second World War and hoped for reform. After Sétif, a generation of nationalists concluded that peaceful politics was hopeless. Nine years later they began the armed struggle with the attacks of 1 November 1954. See also the Algerian War.
